title: Common-driver-resistant control benchmark -- the P4 blocker from 2026-08-27's adversarial null failure
notes: Direct follow-up to adversarial-shared-event-null-failure-20260827.json: ordinary trial-shuffle permutation gave a 100% false-positive rate (10/10 seeds) against a synthetic system with a shared per-trial timing jitter E_i driving both P (LFP proxy) and R (spike proxy), with explicitly ZERO true P->R coupling. Per Hamm's 2026-08-28 instruction, three candidate controls were built and adversarially benchmarked against BOTH a negative control (jitter only, coupling_strength=0 -- must NOT be flagged significant) and a positive control (jitter + a genuine P->R coupling term at a known 30ms lag, coupling_strength=1.2 -- must be flagged AND recover a lag near 30ms). Code: omission/jnwb_ext/common_driver_control.py, omission/tests/test_common_driver_control.py. Final benchmark: n=10 seeds per condition per method, 200 permutations per trial-shuffle p-value. Raw results: common_driver_control_benchmark_20260828.json.
RESULT TABLE (neg_fp_rate = fraction of 10 negative-control seeds flagged p<0.05, should be near alpha=0.05; pos_tp_rate = fraction of 10 positive-control seeds flagged p<0.05, should be near 1.0):
raw (uncorrected trial-shuffle):            neg_fp_rate=1.00  pos_tp_rate=1.00  -- reproduces the 2026-08-27 finding exactly as this benchmark's own internal baseline.

Candidate A, event_template_residualize (cross-validated group-average template subtraction, no per-trial timing estimate): neg_fp_rate=1.00  pos_tp_rate=1.00 -- FAILS the negative control, as predicted: it only removes the AVERAGE evoked shape locked to the nominal/observed event time, not each trial's own hidden jitter deviation from that average, so the shared-jitter-driven correlation survives entirely in the residuals.

Candidate B, reference_peak_realign (per-trial timing estimated via raw single-sample argmax on P, both P and R realigned by that estimate): neg_fp_rate=1.00  pos_tp_rate=1.00 -- ALSO FAILS. Diagnosed root cause (not merely observed): argmax's own estimation error against this broad, low-curvature Gaussian kernel under this noise level has SD~12.7ms, which EXCEEDS the true jitter SD (8ms) it was meant to remove -- so the 'correction' barely changes the confound magnitude at all. This is a concrete, quantified reason a plausible-sounding fix can still fail, not just a restated negative result.

Candidate B2, matched_filter_peak_realign (per-trial timing estimated via cross-validated matched-filter cross-correlation against a group-average P template, both P and R realigned by that estimate): neg_fp_rate=0.00  pos_tp_rate=0.50 -- the ONLY method of the four that passes the negative control (0/10 false positives, vs 10/10 for every other method). Estimator precision check: matched-filter timing estimate correlates r=0.96 with the true (synthetic-only, never used by any method) jitter, residual estimation error SD=2.4ms (vs argmax's 12.7ms) -- confirms precision, not luck, is what fixed the negative control.

POWER COST, quantified and NOT glossed over: Candidate B2's positive-control detection rate (0.50) is far below raw's (1.00) at the SAME injected coupling strength (1.2) -- fixing the false-positive problem cost real sensitivity. A follow-up sweep (n=5 seeds per point, less precise but directionally clear) at coupling_strength in {1.2, 2.5, 4.0} gave TP rates {0.4, 0.4, 0.8} -- power recovers substantially with a ~3.3x stronger injected effect, confirming Candidate B2 is not blind to real coupling (a required sanity check before trusting a 'passes negative control' result), but IS meaningfully underpowered relative to the uncorrected estimator at moderate effect sizes.

Recovered lag for Candidate B2 under the positive control clustered tightly at 35-38ms across all 10 seeds (including the non-significant ones) -- consistently close to, but biased ~6-8ms above, the true injected 30ms lag. Plausible source of this bias: R still contains its own r_indep(t; r_center+E_i, r_sigma) component (the SAME shared-jitter-driven confound term, not coupling) alongside the coupling term; after realignment removes most of the jitter, r_indep's own fixed (average, non-jitter) offset from p_center may still exert a small pull on the composite peak location. Not yet isolated/corrected -- flagged as an open item, not fixed here.

Direct implication: Candidates A and the naive (argmax) version of B are DISQUALIFIED as P4 controls -- confirmed unable to distinguish the shared-jitter confound from real coupling, at the exact benchmark that matters. Candidate B2 (matched-filter realignment) is the only tested method that currently passes the negative control, and is the current leading candidate for the P4 estimator's confound control, but its reduced power at moderate coupling strengths and its small positive lag bias both need to be characterized further (and, ideally, independently improved -- e.g. a matched filter using a better template, more permutations, or a joint model rather than a two-step realign-then-test pipeline) before being adopted as the sole P4 control. Approach C (Hamm's 'event/timing-conditioned permutation or matching', as a null-construction strategy distinct from realignment) has not yet been implemented/tested separately -- Candidate B2 satisfies its spirit (conditioning the test on an estimated timing covariate) but a dedicated matched-permutation-null variant has not been built.

issues.description: Candidate B2 (the only method that passes the negative control) detects true coupling in only 5/10 seeds at the originally-specified moderate effect size (coupling_strength=1.2), versus 10/10 for every method that fails the negative control. This is a real, not cosmetic, cost of the fix.
issues.action: before P4 adopts this as the primary confound control, either improve its power (better template estimation, adaptive max_shift, more permutation power, or a joint likelihood-based approach instead of realign-then-test) or explicitly report the estimator's power curve alongside any null real-data result so a non-significant P4 finding cannot be silently read as 'no coupling' when it may just be 'underpowered against this control'. Not fixed in this build.

issues.description: Recovered lag under the positive control (35-38ms) is consistently ~6-8ms above the true injected 30ms lag, plausibly from the still-present r_indep confound component pulling the composite correlation peak.
issues.action: not yet isolated or corrected; flag alongside any P4 lag estimate derived from this method until characterized further.

verification.status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-28) -- independent verifier ran two passes. Pass 1 (fresh seeds 6001-9006, n_perm=50, none overlapping this session's 1-20): negative control 0/5 significant for matched_filter_realign vs 5/5 for raw/template_residualize/argmax_realign; positive control 2/5 clearly significant + 1 borderline for matched_filter_realign vs 5/5 raw. Pass 2 (fresh seeds 9001-9008, n_perm=200 -- matching this session's own methodology exactly): NEG raw FP rate 1.00 (8/8, p=0.00498 every seed); NEG matched-filter FP rate 0.00 (8/8, p in [0.10,0.92]); POS raw TP rate 1.00 (8/8); POS matched-filter TP rate 0.50 (4/8, p in {0.0050,0.0050,0.040,0.040,0.11,0.20,0.32,0.34}) -- matches this session's claimed 0.50 exactly, not just approximately. Line-by-line trace of the fold-based CV logic in both event_template_residualize and matched_filter_peak_realign confirmed no trial ever contributes to its own template/shift estimate (train/test index sets are disjoint by construction), and confirmed R_trials is never referenced during shift ESTIMATION (only P), ruling out circularity. A 200-seed check confirmed n_folds=5 over n_trials=60 never produces an empty fold bucket. The argmax-vs-matched-filter estimation-error diagnostic was independently re-derived against ground-truth jitter with different seeds and gave different exact numbers (SD 9.5ms vs 2.8ms, vs this session's 12.7ms vs 2.4ms) but the same direction and ratio, corroborating the mechanism, not just the headline number. Power-scaling reconfirmed in pass 2's own fresh seeds: 0/4 significant at coupling_strength=1.2, 4/4 at coupling_strength=4.0. Checked for np.roll wraparound/edge-effect contamination of the null computation specifically (the realignment shifts are all small relative to trial length and kernel positions are far from the trial edges) -- no artifact found; confirmed the identical pre-transform is applied to both the observed and null (permuted) statistic, so there is no asymmetric contamination that could artificially deflate the null.
verification.self_verification_done: diagnosed (not merely observed) why raw argmax realignment failed via a direct estimation-error measurement (SD comparison against true jitter, using ground-truth jitter values available only in the synthetic harness, never exposed to any candidate method); confirmed the matched-filter fix's precision via the same ground-truth comparison (r=0.96, residual SD=2.4ms) before trusting its negative-control pass; ran a positive-control power-scaling sanity check (three coupling strengths) to confirm the method is not simply insensitive to all coupling, before accepting the 0.50 TP rate as a real (not degenerate) result; increased from an initial n=5-seed pass to a final n=10-seed benchmark for the headline numbers reported here.
